ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle SRT, point S is on the left, R is above, and T is at the lower right. There is one identical pink tick mark on each of side SR and side ST, indicating SR = ST. Next to side RT is marked length 14. Segment SX connects from S to point X on side RT, and there is a right-angle mark at X, indicating SX is perpendicular to RT. Reasoning: Because SR = ST, triangle SRT is an isosceles triangle with RT as the base. In an isosceles triangle, the altitude SX drawn from vertex S to base RT is also the median of the base, so X is the midpoint of RT. Given RT = 14, so XT = 14 ÷ 2 = 7.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle SRT with matching tick marks on SR and ST, indicating SR = ST. The side RT is labeled 14, and segment SX meets RT at X with a right-angle mark, so SX is an altitude to RT. Since SR = ST, triangle SRT is isosceles with base RT; in an isosceles triangle, the altitude from the vertex between the equal sides to the base also bisects the base. Therefore X is the midpoint of RT, so XT = 14/2 = 7.
